name: Healthcare AI data governance
description: Reference Trust Requirements Profile for an AI system processing protected health information. Illustrative draft values, not certified compliance thresholds.

scope.intended_use: Trust requirements for an AI system that accesses, processes, or generates outputs from protected health information.
scope.boundary: One AI workflow operating on PHI within a single covered entity or business associate relationship.
out_of_scope: How the system is scored against these signals
How a halt or other action is enforced
Clinical decision-making or FDA device classification

scored_signals.reason: Low confidence in de-identification increases re-identification risk for patient data.
Records processed without verified consent or authorization basis create compliance exposure.
Performance disparity across demographic subgroups indicates bias risk in clinical or operational use.
Stale data may not reflect current patient status or updated records.
Incomplete access logs prevent audit trail reconstruction required by HIPAA.
Low confidence outputs should not be used for decisions affecting patient care or records.

standing_bands.range: All signals within acceptable range, all hard rules satisfied, HIPAA basis verified.
One or more signals in warning range; human review required before continued processing.
A signal in critical range or a hard rule met; PHI processing must stop.

required_standing.source_requirement: For audit or regulatory use, the evaluation source should be independent of the covered entity.

notes: Threshold values are illustrative draft values, not certified compliance thresholds.
Standing bands describe how standing is expressed; they do not define how it is computed.
This profile is a reference template. Real deployments should set values based on institutional policy, applicable state law, and data-source contracts.
Based on preliminary healthcare governance research by the AI Trust Alliance applied research program.
